source.publisher: Northern Whig (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: votes and majority as printed: 'AUGHNACLOY COUNTY DIVISION. Arthur H. Coote (Unionist), 692; James Welsh (Farmers' Union), 659; Unionist majority, 33' (Northern Whig, 3 June 1927). The Ulster Herald of 4 June prints the same votes but a majority line of '53'; 692-659=33 and the News-Letter and Whig both print 33. Citation confirmed 6 Nov 2026: all surnames and most figures found in the page text.

note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, polled Wednesday 1 June 1927. Nominations were taken on Wednesday 20 April 1927, and the Derry Journal of 22 April 1927 prints the full county list division by division under 'Tyrone County and Rural Elections: List of Nominations'. It says 'Only three contests are threatened for the County Council' — Fintona, Aughnacloy and Carrickmore — but the result reports of 2 and 3 June record only two polls, so the Carrickmore challenger withdrew. Killeter is given in the article's text rather than the list, where no nomination was made and Mr. Robert Thompson continued. That makes twenty-six divisions. Dungannon does not appear in the 1927 list at all, although it appears in the 1930 and later returns; it was therefore not a county division at this election, and no member is invented for it. The polled divisions keep the recorded results of 1 June, with the nomination notice added as a second citation. One discrepancy is left on the record: the Belfast Telegraph of 2 June 1927 gives the new council as 25 Unionists and 10 Nationalists — thirty-five members — which is more than the twenty-six divisions printed here, while the Irish News of 10 June 1930 gives twenty-four. The council's total membership is therefore not settled by the sources read, though every division printed is recorded. Coote was the outgoing Unionist member and son of the late Mr. Wm. Coote, M.P.; Welsh stood as the Farmers' Union nominee. The Ulster Herald of 4 June prints the total poll as 1,500 with 14 spoiled votes; that does not reconcile with the votes (1,351 valid + 14 spoiled = 1,365), so the poll figure is left out.
